intro.data: Look up a user's email, then look up that email's host. Each lookup returns a BOX (it might fail). 'bind' chains them: run the first, then feed its contents into the next, flattening the result. Pick the honest lookup (one fabricates an email) and the bind that truly works on what's in the box (one ignores it). Build the chain that finds the real host.
intro.alchemy: Distill a herb into its essence, then distill that essence into its salt. Each step returns a VIAL (it might come up empty). 'bind' chains them: run the first, feed its contents into the next, merging the result. Pick the honest step (one invents an essence) and the bind that works on the real contents. Build the chain to the true salt.
intro.spellcraft: Divine a rune's omen, then divine that omen's sign. Each step returns a CHARM (it might fizzle). 'bind' chains them: run the first, feed its contents into the next, merging the result. Pick the honest step (one invents an omen) and the bind that works on the real contents. Build the chain to the true sign.
intro.abstract: Compose two Kleisli arrows f : A → T(B) and (bind g) : T(B) → T(C). Pick the faithful f and the faithful bind so the value reaches the goal in T(C). Impostors fabricate or ignore the box's contents.

goal.data: Chain the two lookups so a user reaches the real host.
goal.alchemy: Chain the two steps so a herb reaches the true salt.
goal.spellcraft: Chain the two steps so a rune reaches the true sign.
goal.abstract: Reach the goal value in T(C) via f then bind g.

afterSuccess.data: You chained two box-returning lookups with bind: it ran the second lookup on the email INSIDE the box, then flattened the result, so the user reached the real host. The impostors fabricated an email or ignored the box's contents — same types, wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You chained two vial-returning steps with bind: it worked on the essence INSIDE the vial, then merged the result. The impostors invented contents or ignored them.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You chained two charm-returning steps with bind: it worked on the omen INSIDE the charm, then merged the result. The impostors faked contents or ignored them.
afterSuccess.abstract: f : A → T(B) then bind g : T(B) → T(C) composed the two Kleisli arrows; bind = join ∘ T(g) runs g on the contents and flattens.

reveal.summary: bind chains a step that returns a box: bind : T(A) → (A → T(B)) → T(B). It maps the step over the box, then flattens (join). Chaining such steps is composition in the 'Kleisli' world of effectful arrows A → T(B).
reveal.programmerAnalogy: user.flatMap(getEmail).flatMap(getHost) — chaining steps that each return an Optional.
